findings.title: Wrong lightness values for embedded post author link
findings.body: The embedded-post meta data link `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a` was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. This both changes the light-theme color from the intended 30% primary to 70% primary and uses the wrong secondary complement for dark themes. It should preserve the original lightness and use the complementary dark value, i.e. `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. As written, the author link becomes too faint in light themes and has incorrect contrast in dark themes.

findings.title: Group member name color no longer matches original light-theme value
findings.body: `.group-member-info .name` was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The original 30% lightness was lost, so in light themes the member name is now much lighter than before, and the dark-theme branch should be the 70% secondary complement. It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`; otherwise the name no longer contrasts with the adjacent `.title` field as originally intended.

findings.title: Mobile group member name uses wrong lightness pair
findings.body: The mobile `.group-member-info .name` rule was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. This alters the light-theme appearance from the original 30% primary lightness and leaves the dark-theme color at 50% secondary instead of the complementary 70%. The rule should use `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))` to preserve the intended hierarchy between `.name` and `.title`.

findings.title: Mobile topic-map heading color changed from 20% to 50%
findings.body: The mobile `.topic-map h3` color was originally `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`, but the PR changes it to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. This makes the light-theme h3 color much lighter than before and also uses the wrong dark-theme complement. The desktop equivalent was correctly changed to primary 20% / secondary 80%; mobile should match with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`. As-is, the mobile h3 headings are visually de-emphasized compared with the previous design.

findings.title: Custom message length color swapped for light and dark themes
findings.body: `.custom-message-length` originally used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, but the PR changes it to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. This inverts the intended pair: the light-theme branch is now much darker, while the dark-theme branch is much lighter. It is also inconsistent with the desktop modal rule, which correctly uses primary 70% / secondary 30%. It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`.

findings.title: Category badge notification still uses primary-only lightness
findings.body: The conversion is incomplete in this file: `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification` still has `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`. On dark themes this still derives the color from `$primary` instead of `$secondary`, so the fix does not apply to this category badge notification and can produce incorrect contrast compared with the other converted badge colors. It should use the same complementary pattern, e.g. `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`.
